title: The mirror and the crowd
learning_goal: On the three-mode model: see a plain generator inherit the data's polarity bias, a built-in mirror fix it at every knob value while augmentation fixes it only where data exist, the budget check stay blind to the mirror, and a crowd law forced onto each snapshot become a spike; meet the two-jury estimator.
takeaway: Build the mirror into the machine, impose crowd laws on the crowd, and never force a crowd law onto each snapshot.
notes: All scenes are ready (D4): no simulation, training or benchmark; every number comes from E1 results already in the repository (experiences/resultats/e1_gissinger.json, the E1 snapshot archives) through data files. The T4 chapter card sits in the 3.2-s lead-in of 07.1 (tier 0 lit, rail at L3, as in 04.1 and 05.1). The level climbs to L4 at 07.5 with no rail beat (ch07 has no checkpoint); the ch08 card then shows the declared side-step L4 -> L3. Predict beats: Q5 in 07.2 (hold 3.0 s) and Q6 in 07.5 (hold 3.0 s), PREDICT on screen. New recurring device: the two shelves (07.1 empty, plain labels only; 07.2 mirror card 'built in, exactly' on the crowd shelf; 07.4 an empty 'budget' slot walled off from the mirror; 07.5 the budget card first hovers over the per-snapshot shelf during the predict beat, is crossed there, then lands on the crowd shelf; 07.6 the crowd shelf is full and the per-snapshot shelf still empty with a question mark, the hook for ch08 and the payoff in 08.6). Changes against the outline, to review: (1) 07.1 explains where A's tilt comes from (runs below the threshold split unevenly) and 07.3 gives the numbers; the cliffhanger is the mirror glyph with a question mark. (2) 07.2 names the two techniques in narration ('data augmentation', 'equivariance') so the author can use the words with the supervisors, shows the mechanism of Proposition 4 on the equivariance card (a mirrored noise point lands on the mirrored snapshot) and says 'each violet snapshot still points one way' rather than 'sits in one whirlpool' (a handful of generated points, 1 or 2 in 4,000 at Γ = 0.85, fall near D = 0). (3) 07.3 plots all 21 Gamma (not only 0.80-0.88) on a log axis, so B's sawtooth shows above the threshold too (0.0203 at 0.93). (4) 07.4 says 'a check of crowd laws' (the degree-3 control identities, critique B4) instead of 'budget check': on the degree-2 identities, which contain the energy budget, C beats A (0.0265 vs 0.0326), so 'A scores best on the budget' would be wrong; the slider p is chalk, not green (a mixing weight is not a control parameter). (5) 07.5 compares model C's bars with the reference outline and morphs C into E (E is C projected, R:699), so the x9 refers to the bars the viewer sees; the formula layer writes the Lipschitz constant of dE/dt, Lip(Ė), not Lip(phi) as in the outline (Corollary 6 needs the Lipschitz constant of L phi), and avoids the generator symbol (B4). (6) 07.6 uses real model C energy changes as the jury votes (no invented numbers), cites R:124 for the trap having occurred in E1, and ends on 'the next tests will tell', which points to 08.5 (E2 success) and 09.4 (E1 mixed result) without overclaiming. Badges: MEASURED (07.1, 07.3), PROVED (07.2 Proposition 4, 07.4 Remark 3.7, 07.5 Corollary 6, 07.6 Example 4.2), each with the E1 confirmation as badge note; none on the question card. No external fact: no web source needed (Proposition 4 is 'classical for equivariant flows' per R:412, shown as a chip). NEW DATA FILES for tools/data_existing.py (foundation engineer; no run, from e1_gissinger.json and the E1 snapshot archives): data/ch07_mirror.json (blocks ref_sym_085, runs, asym, check3; 07.1-07.4) and data/ch07_spike.json (blocks distance, spread, also_worse, juries; 07.5-07.6), specified in the visuals of 07.1, 07.3, 07.4 and 07.5. Data caveat for the foundation engineer: ref|<Γ> in data/e1_samples_<Γ>.json is the first 8000 rows of the symmetrized reference array, i.e. only the unsymmetrized half (p_positive 0.5625 at 0.85, 0.564 at 0.9): harmless for dE/dt histograms (dE/dt is S-invariant) but misleading for any (Q, D) cloud or polarity count below the threshold (hence ref_sym_085); the site's Figure 7 draws the same subset in grey. Question card: Q8 'framing', born from 07.5-07.6 (the spike, the hidden variance penalty) and the E2 metrics lesson (R:1035); it asks which budgets (energy, cross or magnetic helicity, T:915) the 3D crowd loss should impose and whether a spread criterion applies in 3D (none in the plan, T:917; tier 1 had 0.8-1.2, T:903), which decides what must be programmed in the 3D evaluation before renting (RECOMMANDATION-CLOUD §0 and §4.1 point 1). Symbol sheet: Gamma spoken as a word; D the dipole; dE/dt kept as in 04.7 for the same histogram (physical time appears only inside dE/dt, never as a bare t; Ė in formulas); 'distribution distance' (amber); q the generated law; v_theta violet; no mu_+/- or generator symbol in the core (formula layers say 'up', 'down', and a dotted phi); no lambda for a growth rate. Words budgeted at 125-130 effective words per minute against target_s; estimates use the assembler formula (146 raw words per minute, 0.9 s per paragraph break, holds, lead-in and tail).

scenes.title: A lopsided machine

sentences.text: Physics hands the machine two kinds of laws.
Some hold for every single snapshot.
Others hold only for the crowd.
Two shelves, still empty.
Back to the three dials, at a {param}Gamma{/} never seen in training.
Grey: true snapshots.
Violet: a plain {model}generator{/}.
The shape is right.
Now weigh the sides.
The truth is balanced; the machine is not.
Only about four in ten of its snapshots point up.
It copied its data: below the threshold, each run stays in one whirlpool, and the runs split unevenly.

predict.question: At a Γ neither has seen, who stays balanced?

sentences.text: Two ways to teach the mirror.
The first student, data augmentation, sees each training snapshot flipped half the time.
The second, equivariance, has the mirror built into its wind: a mirrored noise point always lands on the mirrored snapshot.
At a {param}Gamma{/} neither has seen, who stays balanced?
The built-in mirror.
The first student tilts a little.
Yet in the mirror's crowd, each snapshot still points one way.
The mirror balances the crowd, not each snapshot.
Its card goes on the crowd shelf: built in, exactly.

scenes.title: Only where the data are

sentences.text: Here is that tilt, setting by setting.
Below the threshold, runs often split unevenly: at zero point eight six, only five of sixteen runs point up.
The plain {model}machine{/} copies the imbalance, and spills it onto unseen settings.
Augmentation sits on the {metric}noise floor{/} at its training settings.
Between them, it drifts: the network fills the gaps freely.
The built-in mirror stays on the floor everywhere.
Flipped copies teach the mirror only where there are data.

sentences.text: Can the energy budget catch the tilt?
No. Each whirlpool balances its own budget.
So a mix of the two passes, in any proportion.
On a check of crowd laws, the most lopsided machine even edges ahead.
The mirror needs its own tool.

scenes.title: Predict: balance every snapshot?

predict.title: PREDICT
predict.question: Force every snapshot to balance exactly: better or worse?

sentences.text: Remember the budget of the shoebox.
Snapshot by snapshot, energy rises or falls.
Only the crowd balances, on average, like a bank account over the years.
Now, a tempting fix for the machine.
Force every generated snapshot to balance its budget exactly. Better, or worse?
Worse.
Push each snapshot until its energy stops changing: the wide pile collapses into a spike at zero.
A ledger where every single day balances.
No real account looks like that.
The {metric}distribution distance{/} to the truth grows ninefold.
A short proof says why: even a perfect generator, forced this way, cannot match the truth.
So the budget goes on the crowd shelf.
On the next test bench, a cruder score is fooled by such a spike.

labels: rate of change of energy, dE/dt
Force every snapshot to balance exactly: better or worse?
next: a test bench with whole fields

formulas.tex: \text{under the truth, } \dot E \text{ has no atom at } 0 \;\Rightarrow\; \text{every law } q_{\text{forced}} \text{ on } \{\dot E = 0\} \text{ is singular: } \mathrm{KL}(q_{\text{forced}}\,\|\,\text{truth}) = \infty\ (\text{infinitely surprised}),\quad W_1(q_{\text{forced}}, \text{truth}) \ge \mathbb{E}_{\text{truth}}|\dot E|\,/\,\mathrm{Lip}(\dot E)\quad(\text{Corollary 6})

scenes.title: Enforce it on the crowd, with two juries

sentences.text: Impose the budget on the crowd, during training.
Draw a batch of snapshots at any {param}Gamma{/}, even without data.
Average their energy change and square it: this penalty vanishes only when the crowd balances.
But there is a trap.
Even for a balanced crowd, a batch's average wobbles; its square grows with the scatter.
So training also squeezes the scatter, nudging every snapshot toward balance: toward the spike.
It showed up while building this experiment.
The fix: split the batch into two independent juries and multiply their averages.
On average, the scatter drops out, leaving only the crowd's imbalance.
Does it pay off? The next tests will tell.

question.en: In 3D, which *budgets* should generated fields meet on average, and must their *spread* match too?
question.say: In three dimensions, which budgets should generated fields meet on average, and must their spread match too?
question.fr: En 3D, quels bilans les champs générés doivent-ils respecter en moyenne, et leur dispersion doit-elle aussi être celle des simulations ?
question.why: A budget forced on each field becomes a spike that a spectrum score misses (E2); even the crowd loss narrowed the spread by a quarter (E1). The 3D plan sets no such criterion, and the 3D evaluation logs mean residuals only.
question.unblocks: Which budgets the 3D crowd loss imposes (energy is coded; cross or magnetic helicity would need code), the spread metric to add to the 3D evaluation before renting, and that run's verdict rule.
question.why_fr: Un bilan imposé à chaque champ devient un pic qu'un score spectral ne voit pas (E2) ; même la perte en loi a resserré la dispersion d'un quart (E1). Le plan 3D ne fixe aucun critère de ce type, et l'évaluation 3D n'enregistre que des résidus moyens.
question.unblocks_fr: Les bilans qu'impose la perte en loi en 3D (l'énergie est codée ; l'hélicité croisée ou magnétique demanderait du code), la métrique de dispersion à ajouter à l'évaluation 3D avant de louer, et la règle de verdict de ce run.
